summary:
Orbit Architect: Deep Space Odyssey is a 3D Mars mission simulator that runs in the browser. It uses Three.js for the graphics and has a futuristic cockpit-style interface. You lead the “Ares Basin Odyssey” mission through five phases:

Blueprint: In the assembly bay you pick the spacecraft parts (command module, power, engines, communications, landing hardware, science tools, rover). You must stay within the budget, weight limit and fuel requirements. An auto-fit button builds a working design for you.
Launch: You run the countdown and respond to timed events such as ignition, stage separation, guidance faults and orbit insertion.
Transfer: You set the engine burn strength and angle to aim at Mars. You then fly the ship by hand through an asteroid belt.
Landing: You deploy the drogue parachute, the main parachute and the landing engines inside narrow altitude and speed windows.
Surface: You drive a rover, collect seven samples and send the data back from near the lander. Dust storms and a solar flare threaten your battery.

Your score and rank feed a career mode with unlockable hardware, a research tree, a mission archive and achievements. The game also has pause, settings and saved progress.
details:
Name: Orbit Architect: Deep Space Odyssey (Ares Basin Odyssey mission)
Type: 3D browser game. It has no build step, just plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
Tech: Three.js 0.160 loaded from a CDN, plus Tailwind from a CDN. The CDN files and Google Fonts need an internet connection.
Entry file: index.html
Server: serve.mjs, an optional Node.js server on port 5173. It now also shows an address you can open on your phone.

Folder structure

  • index.html: all screens and menus (lobby, mission control, the 5 phases, report, settings)
  • css/style.css: original desktop look
  • css/mobile.css: new, phone layout and touch-control styling
  • css/trace.css: small telemetry graph styles
  • js/main.js: the main game logic for all phases
  • js/ui.js: screen updates and button wiring
  • js/state.js: settings, saves, build math and scoring
  • js/catalog.js: parts, destinations, research tree and mission numbers
  • js/audio.js: sound
  • js/difficulty.js: new, Easy / Medium / Hard values
  • js/touch.js: new, joystick and on-screen buttons
  • js/three/: the 3D scenes, one per phase (assembly bay, launch, orbit, asteroids, landing, surface, menu)
  • ares-horizon.html: a separate older rover game, untouched

Gameplay

Five phases: Blueprint, Launch, Transfer (with an asteroid belt), Landing and Surface. Progress, settings and career data are saved in the browser’s local storage.

What I changed

  • Phone layout: a compact landscape view and a “rotate your phone” prompt in portrait. Graphics default to Medium on phones.
  • Touch controls: a joystick plus BOOST, COLLECT and UPLINK buttons, and a HUD show/hide button.
  • Difficulty: Easy, Medium (the default) and Hard (the original game), chosen at Mission Control or in Settings.
  • Sharing: a HOW-TO-PLAY-ON-PHONE.txt file with setup steps.

Status

I checked the code for errors but have not run it on a real phone. Your testing feedback is the next step.
